extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of philosophy (Plato's Republic); people studying ideal education and political theory
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and standards for educating, testing, selecting, and provisioning the guardian class in an ideal city (Plato's Republic). Covers music and gymnastic training, selection trials, professional suitability, communal living, and limits on property and luxury.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primacy of musical training
rubrics_metrics.description: Musical training is a more potent instrument than any other, because rhythm and harmony find their way into the inward places of the soul, imparting grace and making the soul graceful or ungraceful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasise early and careful musical education; music shapes taste so that the educated will perceive omissions or faults in art and nature, praise and receive the good, and blame the bad even before they can articulate reasons. Music's ultimate end is the love of beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know essential moral forms before musical education
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither guardians nor their educators can become musical until they know the essential forms of temperance, courage, liberality, magnificence, and their contraries, in all combinations, so they can recognize these forms wherever found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach moral categories (virtues and vices) in parallel with musical training; do not slight these forms whether in small or great instances—recognition across contexts is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity in music (avoid complex panharmonies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple music is parent of temperance in the soul; complexity in musical styles engenders licence and moral disorder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer straightforward, temperate musical modes and melodies; avoid panharmonic/overly complex rhythms and soft, excessively soothing airs that can soften and waste spirit (leading to effeminacy or feebleness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gymnastic training from early years and lifelong
rubrics_metrics.description: Gymnastics should begin in early years, be careful in training, and continue through life — especially military gymnastic designed to produce wakeful, keen-sensed warriors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design a regimen that produces endurance across climate/food/water changes in campaigns; avoid athlete-style regimens that create bulky, inactive habits and susceptibility to illness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity in gymnastic (military-oriented)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a simple, good gymnastic—especially the military gymnastic—that, like simple music, produces health and temperance; refined food/luxuries undermine this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ban elaborate culinary refinements (e.g., Syracusan dinners, Athenian confections) and distractions (luxurious companions) for those training as guardians; prefer diets and practices that are practical for soldiers (roast rather than boiled, simple fare).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between music and gymnastic
rubrics_metrics.description: True education mixes music and gymnastic in fairest proportions to harmonize the spirited and philosophical elements; guardians should have both gentleness and courage in harmony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid exclusive devotion to either: too much gymnastic yields brutality and ignorance; too much music yields softness and wasted spirit. The ideal educator tempers both to produce a harmonious soul (temperate and courageous).

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardians must abstain from intoxication
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians should abstain from getting drunk; a guardian should be the last to get intoxicated and lose himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce sobriety as a moral and practical requirement for those entrusted with public safety and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of medicine and limits on medicalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Medicine should treat definite ailments in otherwise useful citizens; it should not 'educate diseases' by promoting valetudinarian lifestyles or prolonging useless lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physicians should supply rough-and-ready cures for working people so they can return to their occupations; avoid extended regimes of dietetics that make a person constantly ill and dependent on care. Do not expend public medical resources preserving lives that contribute nothing to the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physicians' experiential qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The most skilful physicians are those who combine knowledge with great personal or observed experience of disease; experience of sickness helps their art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer physicians acquainted with many constitutions and ailments—but the text also warns against a physician whose whole life is consumed in valetudinarianism; calibrate experience with competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges' moral and experiential qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The judge governs mind by mind and therefore ought not to have been trained among vicious minds; he should not have personal contamination by vice from youth but should know vice by late and long observation of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select judges who are mature, honourable, and learned about evil through observation rather than personal practice; avoid appointing those who have committed many crimes and learned cunning by experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of excessive attention to bodily regimen among the rich
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive care of the body, carried beyond gymnastic rules, is inimical to the practice of virtue and to duties (management, study, self-reflection); it breeds illnesses and dependence on physicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourage indulgent regimens among the wealthy that produce constant ailments; encourage active civic/occupational engagement as the best safeguard for health and virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection tests for guardians across ages
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians must be watched at every age and tested by actions likely to make them forget or be deceived; tests should include ordeals, toils, conflicts, terrors, and pleasures to discover who keeps conviction and duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct staged trials analogous to taking colts amid noise, exposing candidates to persuasion (theft), force, and enchantment (pleasure/fear). Select those who remain steadfast at boyhood, youth, and maturity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define 'theft, force, enchantment' as causes of losing conviction
rubrics_metrics.description: Loss of resolution can occur willingly (by shedding false beliefs) or unwillingly through theft (persuasion), force (violence/pain/grief), or enchantment (deception via pleasure or fear).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design tests that separately probe susceptibility to argument-based persuasion, coercion, and allure/terror to ensure robustness of civic conviction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointments, honours, and rejection policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who pass all trials at every age shall be appointed rulers and guardians and honoured in life and death; those who fail are to be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make selection binary and consequential—successful candidates receive highest honours and burial; failures are excluded from rulership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commune of goods and prohibition on private property for guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians should have no private property beyond necessities, no private houses or closed stores; their provisions should suffice for trained warriors only; they should accept a fixed pay and live together in communal messes like soldiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibit guardians from owning or handling gold/silver, wearing or drinking from them, or ever being under the same roof with such wealth. Limit pay to annual needs so guardians won't become housekeepers, husbandmen, enemies or tyrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing and provisioning suited to soldier-guardians
rubrics_metrics.description: Guardians' dwellings must be those of soldiers (shelter from elements) and not shopkeepers; their environment should neither impair virtue nor tempt them to prey on other citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design barracks-style housing and communal provisioning to avoid temptations of private wealth or luxury. Physical arrangements should support discipline and civic-mindedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breeding and social origins (the 'royal lie' and purity of race)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a founding myth (the 'royal lie') that citizens are born of the earth and have metals mixed in their souls (gold, silver, brass/iron); rulers must guard the purity of the race and oversee transpositions of rank when mixtures appear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ civic myth-making to foster solidarity and acceptance of social functions; monitor offspring for dispositions and reassign ranks as nature and mixtures dictate to preserve the city's stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of arts (music/gymnastic) is soul improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Music and gymnastic are not primarily for pleasure or bodily excellence but chiefly for improving the soul; teachers should aim at shaping character, not mere technical skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame curricula of music and physical training around cultivating temperance, courage, and harmony in the soul rather than virtuosity or bodily spectacle.
